analysis: Examined the two base-side excerpts (lines 10757-12403) of fixtures/prompt-contract/v1/production_vectors.json. Contents shown are synthetic text ("summarize", "Public synthetic cache-parity input"), tool schemas, and token IDs. No secrets, credentials, keys, attestation material or consumer data appear. The patch excerpt (truncated, not complete) shows head-side changes: an added additional_context {enable_thinking:false} in template_input, changed prompt_token_count (803->767), changed block-boundary chain hashes, and removed token IDs. These are expected vector regeneration for a prompt-template change. Related to T-041 (prefix-cache chain hashes), but changed chain hashes only reflect new tokenization; the excerpts show no weakening of cache keying, tenant scoping, encryption or authorization (TB-011/A-016 unaffected). The fixture is test data, so no runtime trust boundary is crossed by this file. The remaining unverified point is whether the Swift/Go code that generates or consumes these vectors (the additional_context handling and the prompt_contract_id) changed in a way that affects cache isolation or template injection. That code is not in the supplied batch. The prompt_contract_id in the base excerpt is 7fa068ec... while the patch shows 8171fec3... for another vector, so the full diff should be checked for consistent contract-ID changes. No concrete regression is identified from the supplied evidence.
